title: How Simon Høiberg built a SaaS factory to test and ship products 10x faster
summary: Simon argues that SaaS is a high-failure game, so the best strategy is to test many products cheaply. He describes the parts of his "SaaS factory": a GitHub org of reusable packages and boilerplates, no-code automation templates, a creative asset library, a launch checklist, and a personal playbook. The factory only works if you build it yourself.

principles.text: Constantly testing new ideas is the best way to raise your odds of SaaS success, given how likely any one product is to fail.
principles.quote: constantly testing the market with new ideas is the best way to increase your chances of success but you need the right tooling to do this sustainably

principles.text: The most successful indie hackers win by pushing and failing more and faster than others.
principles.quote: the reason they're successful is that they've been pushing and failing more and faster than most other people

principles.text: Turn reusable code into private packages and boilerplates so new products start from a working base in under 30 minutes.
principles.quote: get into the habit of stopping regularly go through your code and pick out pieces that you know or at least feel very sure could be reused

principles.text: Use both code and no-code: automate non-core backend work like segmentation, retargeting lists and social updates, and reuse the automations across products.
principles.quote: people have this idea that it's either code or no code but in order to build a proper SAS Factory you should have both

principles.text: Keep a checklist for every new SaaS (payments, email, auth, privacy policy, terms) and document your processes, as quality control.
principles.quote: every time you set up a new SAS make sure you can cross everything on the list consider this quality control

principles.text: Build your own factory and playbook rather than buying someone else's; the learning from building it is the real advantage.
principles.quote: what truly gives you superpowers is the process of building the factory all the hard-earned lessons that make up the foundation you're building on
